transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what brought me in is that... well, some nights after work, or maybe after a really tense dinner, I start eating and it just feels like the decision-making part of me shuts off. It's like I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but I just can't make myself stop.
Can you describe what you mean by not being able to stop yourself once you start eating? Does it feel like you're losing control over how much you eat or when you stop?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I was just saying, it really does feel like I lose complete control over how much I'm having and when to quit. Um, once I get going, it's like my brain just checks out. I know I've had enough, and I can physically see my hand grabbing another handful of whatever it is, but I just... I can't force myself to put it down. The off-switch just completely disappears.
Does this feeling of losing control only happen during specific situations, like after tense dinners or work, or does it also happen at other times when you're eating?

It's mostly just in those specific situations, honestly. I don't really have that feeling of losing control when I'm just eating a normal lunch at work or having breakfast. It's usually just when I'm stressed or overwhelmed, like after a long shift or if things are tense at home. Other times, I can just eat a normal amount and stop without a problem.
Do these episodes of feeling out of control while eating cause you significant distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Well, I wouldn't say it stops me from functioning entirely. I mean, I'm still showing up for my cashier shifts and taking care of my normal responsibilities just fine. But... yeah, it does interfere. 

I've actually started avoiding some family meals after work. Or if I am around them, I'm just acting really distracted. I get so caught up worrying about what I just ate, or, you know, figuring out what I'm going to do to compensate for it. So it definitely takes a toll on my personal life and my peace of mind.

After these episodes where you feel out of control while eating, do you ever try to compensate for it by doing something like exercising a lot, making yourself vomit, or restricting your food intake later?

Yeah... I do. Usually, it's late, like after everyone else has gone to bed. I'll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up. Or sometimes I'll take laxatives. I always tell myself I'm just doing it to undo the damage from what I ate. But honestly, afterward, I just feel really embarrassed... and kind of shaky. It's not something I'm proud of.
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit or using laxatives after these eating episodes, and is it mainly because you're worried about gaining weight or how your body looks?

Well, for the last few months, it's been happening most weeks. I'll have one of those out-of-control nights, and then... yeah, I try to make up for it. I'll throw up, or take the laxatives, or sometimes I'll just skip meals the next day or force myself to go on a really long walk. 

And, yes, it is mainly because I'm worried about gaining weight. I just... I don't want to get bigger, and I get so anxious about what all that food is going to do to my body. So I feel like I have to get rid of it.
When these episodes happen, do you feel a sense of marked distress about the eating behavior, and does the eating itself occur in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours?

Yeah, I definitely feel distressed about it. It's... it's really upsetting. And yes, it happens pretty fast. On bad nights, I can eat a full plate of leftovers, and then... well, then I just keep going. I'll go through bread, snacks, ice cream in the kitchen, all within an hour or two. It's way more food than I'd ever eat if someone were sitting there with me. It just all happens so quickly.
Can you tell me if during these episodes you feel like you’re unable to stop eating or control what or how much you’re eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. That's actually what brought me in to see someone. Some nights, usually after I get off work or maybe after a tense dinner, I start eating and it just feels like the decision-making part of me completely shuts off. It's a weird feeling... I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but I just can't make myself stop. I really have no control over it once it starts.
Do these episodes of feeling out of control while eating usually happen when you're alone, or do they also occur in front of other people?

It almost always happens when I'm alone. Like I said, I'd never eat that much if someone was sitting right there with me. I usually wait until my roommate is asleep or out for the night. If someone is around, I can usually hold it together, or at least eat a normal amount. It's really only when I'm by myself that the control completely goes out the window.
Do these episodes usually happen when you're not physically hungry, and do you feel unable to control how much you eat even if you know you don't need to eat that much?

I haven't really noticed if my stomach is actually empty or anything when it happens. I'm not really sure if it's actual physical hunger. I mean, I might be a little hungry if I just got off a long shift at the register, but definitely not hungry enough to need all that food. I know I don't need to eat that much, but... yeah, like I was saying a minute ago, I still just can't seem to stop myself once I start.

No prior candidates existed.
